policy: delete-with-gaps (no renumber); ADR numbers are stable identifiers (RFC discipline)

entries.title: BANZA as Open Financial Protocol
entries.rationale: The founding decision — BANZA is an operator-neutral open financial protocol, operators are implementations — is exactly current policy and is load-bearing (cited by ADR-003/004/005/033 and CLAUDE.md). But the body is written in operator-extraction voice ('Banza began as a single private fintech product', 'the reference operator becomes clearly one operator'), the author frontmatter is operator-as-subject ('the reference operator Organisation'), and it carries a 2026-07 'Current protocol boundary note' tombstone. Clean-slate: keep the decision, rewrite the body to state the operator-neutral protocol cleanly, fix the author, drop the tombstone.

entries.title: Ecosystem Naming Inversion
entries.contradiction_detail: No hard contradiction, but the ADR repeatedly treats an operator as the subject ('the reference operator becomes the name of the first and main product', product-vs-protocol name tables), which is against the operator-neutral framing even though the durable naming output is correct.
entries.rationale: The durable core (BANZA = protocol / BanzAI = AI-layer canonical names; permanent @banza IDENTITY_NAMESPACE; protected names) is current and is not restated by any other ADR, so not DELETE. But the document is dominated by an operator-era naming-migration narrative with operator-as-subject product tables, a compatibility/transition period, and pointers to migration working docs (docs/migration/*) that no longer exist. Rewrite to a clean operator-neutral naming + namespace decision and drop the inversion/migration narrative. (Arguably SPLIT the permanent @banza namespace into its own ADR.)

entries.title: Protocol/Operator Separation
entries.removed_detail: Body references reference/sandbox-operator/ and operator-specific provider integrations (EMIS/Multicaixa/Firebase) that are not present in the protocol-only repo; these are illustrative-only per the 2026-07 boundary note, so the decision itself is not removed.
entries.rationale: The decision (protocol defines traits + invariants, operators implement providers) is current and canonical (CLAUDE.md ADR-003 = 'Operator separation'). But the author frontmatter is operator-as-subject ('the reference operator Organisation'), the provider table names operator-specific integrations (EMIS/Multicaixa/Firebase) and a removed reference/sandbox-operator/, and a 2026-07 boundary-note tombstone patches this in prose. Rewrite operator-neutrally (Operator A/B/C trait examples), fix the author, and fold/drop the tombstone.

entries.title: Reference Operator
entries.removed_detail: operator-as-subject / removed sandbox: reference/sandbox-operator, reference/local-ledger, reference/mock-routing, reference/simulated-settlement, reference/fake-acquirer and the docker-compose runtime no longer exist in the protocol-only repo — the ADR's own 2026-07 historical note states this is 'no longer the repository architecture'.
entries.merge_or_supersede_target: ADR-052 (Operador Zero reference payment-operator simulator) + ADR-053 (Operator-Zero-only demo/example policy)
entries.rationale: The ADR describes removed architecture — a runnable sandbox-operator playground (local ledger, mock routing, simulated settlement, fake acquirer, docker compose) that the protocol-only repo no longer contains; the ADR's own historical note admits removal. Its one live concept — a single official reference/example operator for developers — is fully covered by ADR-052 (Operador Zero canonical reference payment-operator simulator, demo-only) and ADR-053 (Operator-Zero-only demo/example policy). Remaining keep-value is purely historical, which Git preserves → DELETE.

entries.title: Protocol-first product development
entries.rationale: Current, coherent, and operator-neutral. Author is 'BANZA Protocol'; the downward-flow rule is exactly the CLAUDE.md 'Regra absoluta' and is explicitly cited there. 'Reference operator' appears only as a role in examples (CLAUDE.md explicitly blesses this — 'the rule names the operator role, not any operator brand'). No CA/root-key/discretionary/operator-as-subject-of-a-protocol-claim content. It references ADR-016 (Collections), which remains a current ADR. KEEP.

entries.title: Double-Entry Ledger and Monetary Precision
entries.rationale: Permanent financial-invariant foundation (INV-LEDGER: double-entry, immutable append-only ledger, i64 minor units, no floats) — substance is untouchable, current, and the opening paragraph is already corrected to operator-neutral wording ('BANZA does not move, hold, settle or custody funds'). The only defect is a redundant 2026-07 'Erratum' tombstone restating that operator-era wording was fixed. Clean-slate mandate (no 'antes o BANZA movia dinheiro' narrative): drop the erratum → light-touch REWRITE; the decision is unchanged. (Borderline KEEP if the erratum is treated as acceptable minor cruft.)

entries.title: Double-Entry Invariant: Enforcement Strategy
entries.rationale: Current invariant-enforcement decision and the natural companion to ADR-006; substance is operator-neutral ('invariants operators can rely on / must uphold'). Defect: author frontmatter is operator-as-subject ('the reference operator Organisation'). Fix the frontmatter (and optionally generalize the Rust-specific PostingBuilder wording as reference-implementation guidance) → REWRITE. Not MERGE into ADR-006 — enforcement strategy is a legitimately distinct decision from the bookkeeping-model decision.

entries.title: Markdown-First Content Architecture — docs/reference/en/complete.md as Single Source of Truth
entries.contradiction_detail: The single-source reference doc is framed around an operator as subject — section titles '## 1. What Is the reference operator?', '## 12. the reference operator for Developers', '## 14. The the reference operator Flywheel' (the last also a botched find/replace) — and the ADR hard-codes a '20 sections' build-validation model that conflicts with the current operator-neutral 14-chapter Reference Information Architecture (M2.7L: PostgreSQL=05, FAQ=14).
entries.rationale: Contradicts operator-neutrality (reference-doc sections make an operator the subject) and is stale (mandates a 20-section model that clashes with the current 14-chapter Reference IA governed by the M2.7L reference-information-architecture-check; no ADR governs that IA today). The core principle — markdown single source rendered by the website — is not restated by any current ADR, so not DELETE. Rewrite operator-neutrally and reconcile the section model with the current Reference IA. (Much of the body is website-implementation detail — lib/reference.ts parsing, React components, routing — so MOVE to docs/ is a defensible alternative.)

entries.title: Provider Abstraction Model
entries.removed_detail:
Not CA/root-key/production-root, but the text describes removed reference-implementation architecture: reference/sandbox-operator/ simulated providers and the banza-acquiring / PostgresAcquiringEngine

/ EMISProvider crates that were dropped in V1 purification (reference implementation removed; BanzAI is knowledge-only).
entries.contradiction_detail: Frontmatter Author is an operator ('the reference operator Organisation' — operator-as-author). The body is a reference-operator implementation design (concrete Rust crates, engines, EMISProvider, sandbox-operator) placed in the operator-neutral protocol ADR set, where the protocol is meant to be technology-neutral for operators. The reference sandbox-operator no longer exists in this repo.
entries.rationale: The underlying decision — protocol integration points are interfaces that operators plug into, so the core depends on no operator/provider — is a legitimate, still-valid neutrality principle distinct from ADR-001/003. But the ADR is dressed entirely in removed reference-implementation detail (banza-acquiring, PostgresAcquiringEngine, EMISProvider, reference/sandbox-operator) and carries operator-as-author frontmatter. Rewrite to state the operator-neutral interface principle without the deleted crates/sandbox-operator and without an operator author.

entries.title: Account/Participant Identity Model (Account-Based, Not Card-First)
entries.contradiction_detail: The binding decision and the 2026-07 Erratum are fully aligned with current policy (BANZA is a protocol, not a wallet/operator). Residual issue is hygiene, not a policy contradiction.
entries.rationale: Live, current, heavily-referenced protocol constraint (ADR-017 extends it) — not DELETE. But the filename still says 'wallet-native-identity' (the pre-erratum framing the title itself abandoned), and the body carries a tombstone-style narrative ('Early operator-era documentation described this as wallet-native' + a separate 2026-07 Erratum) that the clean-slate wants absorbed into clean current text. Rewrite: rename file to the account/participant-identity title and fold the erratum into the current body, dropping the 'previously wallet-native' narrative.

entries.title: Idempotency and Rate Limiting with Redis
entries.contradiction_detail: Prescribes operator implementation technology (Redis, api-gateway/core-api topology, ZADD/ZREMRANGEBYSCORE, tokio, numeric limits 1000/60 req-min, 'save 60 1') inside an operator-neutral protocol repo whose policy is explicitly technology-neutral for operators. The one genuine protocol requirement (replay-safe idempotency) is already owned by the INV-IDEM-* invariant family; rate limiting is not a protocol invariant at all.
entries.merge_or_supersede_target: Protocol idempotency requirement already covered by INV-IDEM-*; the Redis/rate-limit/gateway content is operator implementation and belongs in the reference operator repo (~/banza) / operator implementation docs, not the protocol's decisions/adr.
entries.scope_note: MOVE→operator-repo not possible cross-repo. REWRITE in place to protocol-level: strip operator implementation tech (Redis/gateway/limits/tokio), state idempotency as INV-IDEM-*; drop rate-limiting-as-protocol framing.
entries.rationale: This is operator/reference-implementation architecture (Redis choice, gateway topology, specific limits, fail-open), not a protocol architecture decision. It also conflates two distinct concerns (idempotency vs rate limiting). Its only protocol-level rule — replay-safe idempotency keyed by (merchant, key) — is already the INV-IDEM invariant. Move the implementation guidance to the reference operator; nothing operator-neutral is lost from the protocol ADR set.

entries.title: QR Code Payment System
entries.contradiction_detail: Operator-as-subject language: 'Banza needs a contactless payment mechanism', 'Banza generates QR payloads in-house' — writes BANZA-the-protocol as the entity that needs and serves payments, exactly the operator framing the ADR-010 erratum removed (BANZA moves no funds). Also carries reference-operator implementation detail (tokio::spawn expiry worker in core-api, raw UPDATE SQL, qr_flutter/qr.js client libs).
entries.rationale: Foundational, still-current protocol primitive: it owns the QR payload spec and static/dynamic semantics and the INV-QR invariant family, and is referenced by ADR-010/014/015/016/017 (ADR-015 generalizes it to DYNAMIC_QR/STATIC_QR interfaces but does not restate the payload spec) — not DELETE or MERGE. Rewrite to remove operator-as-subject 'Banza' phrasing and the tokio/SQL/client-library implementation detail, keeping the operator-neutral QR protocol semantics.

entries.title: Payment Links: Shareable URL Commerce Primitive
entries.contradiction_detail: Operator-as-subject language ('Banza needs a zero-friction payment primitive', 'the Banza app', 'a registered Banza account') writes the protocol as a payment product. Body is a reference-operator product design: pay.banza.network domain, Next.js apps/pay App Router, 3s polling of GET /public/pay/{slug}/status — operator implementation, not protocol.
entries.rationale: The payment-link concept is a live protocol surface, referenced by ADR-010/014/015/016 (a surface/interface of PaymentIntent/Session) and not restated by them — not DELETE or MERGE. But the ADR is written as an operator product (pay page stack, polling, operator domain) with operator-as-subject phrasing. Rewrite to state the operator-neutral payment-link primitive (slug URL, fixed/open, resolves to a payment session) and drop the Next.js/pay-page/polling implementation.

entries.title: Payment Intent: the canonical payment-initiation primitive
entries.rationale: Current, coherent, operator-agnostic and correctly framed: PaymentIntent never holds/moves money, ledger untouched, certification expressed as a capability (supports_payment_intents = Level-2, deterministic/evidence-based), INV-TRACE-001 honoured. Full, well-formed frontmatter (Author BANZA Protocol). No CA/discretionary/operator-as-subject issues. Foundational money object that ADR-015 and ADR-016 both build on — keep as-is.

entries.title: Payment Session: the unified payment interface
entries.rationale: Current, operator-neutral, normative invariants correctly stated ('the operator resolves it', apps never generate authoritative financial payloads, no new money object, ledger untouched). No CA/discretionary/operator-as-subject problems. Tightly coupled to ADR-014 but distinct (014 = the money object; 015 = the multi-interface binding + segregated-account destination), and it does not restate the QR/link payload specs — keep. Minor, non-blocking: the Rollout/Operators text cites 'the reference operator's ADR-017' (a cross-repo operator ADR distinct from this repo's ADR-017), which could be clarified on any future touch but is not a policy contradiction.

entries.title: Payment Collections (split / shared / group payments)
entries.contradiction_detail: The Interoperability section names the future cross-operator path as 'the federation contracts (contracts/federation/*, ADR-026/ADR-027)'. ADR-026 (Federation Trust Model) and ADR-027 (Production Root Architecture) are the removed CA-era / production-root architecture, superseded by ADR-038/ADR-040. The current federation-trust path is ADR-040 (federation trust evaluation without certificates). Pointing future federation work at the removed CA/production-root ADRs contradicts current policy.
entries.rationale: The Collections model itself is excellent, current, deterministic, operator-agnostic and invariant-clean (INV-COLLECTION-*, no ledger primitive, no balance, no discretionary actor) — strong live rule, not DELETE/MERGE. Only defect is the stale federation cross-reference to the removed CA-era ADR-026/ADR-027; rewrite that single reference to the current ADR-040 (and ADR-038/039) so the future cross-operator path points at the certificate-free federation model.

entries.title: Wallet/account merchant payments and refund source model
entries.rationale: Live protocol-level financial modelling rule, fully operator-neutral ('BANZA defines the model; operators implement it'), preserves double-entry (ADR-006/007). No CA, root-key, discretionary approval, or operator-as-subject. The 2026-07 Erratum correctly clarifies BANZA is not a wallet and does not custody/move funds — aligned with current policy. Only cosmetic tightening possible; keep as-is.

entries.title: Merchant-facing refundable-source reference on paid payment events
entries.scope_note: MOVE→docs deferred; keep in place. Minimal fix only: correct the broken 'ADR-021 (proof state)'→ADR-023 reference. Non-normative draft tolerated in-tree.
entries.rationale: By its own frontmatter this is 'NOT NORMATIVE / NOT SUBMITTED' and 'decides nothing' — it is a discussion draft/RFC, not an architecture decision, and lists five open governance questions. It does not belong in decisions/adr in a current-only canonical tree. It is not removed architecture (so not DELETE) and its open question (refund-source exposure; TRANSACTION vs ACQUIRING_PAYMENT naming) may still be live, so MOVE to a docs/ proposals/RFC location. Note: it mis-cites 'ADR-021 (Proof state after partial restitution)' — proof-state semantics live in ADR-023, not the conformance-level ADR-021 — a broken reference to fix on move.

entries.title: Generic Fee & Application-Settlement Architecture
entries.contradiction_detail: Uses non-neutral operator-product example names — an on-demand commerce app 'Mongo' (line 143, appears only in this ADR) and the 'DOA' donation application — instead of the mandated Operator A / generic examples, breaching the operator-neutrality invariant (policy 1) and identity-check. The fee/settlement decision itself is policy-compliant and double-entry-safe.
entries.rationale: Decision is current, sound, operator-neutral in substance (no percentages in protocol; double-entry preserved; no CA/root-key/discretionary/operator-as-subject). REWRITE only to genericize the product-specific example names ('Mongo', 'DOA') to Operator A / neutral application examples so the ADR is operator-neutral end to end.

entries.title: Wallet Accounts (Segregated Accounts within a Wallet)
entries.contradiction_detail: References operator-specific product/console names — the 'DOA' donation application and 'BANZADMIN' admin console (line 141, appears only in this ADR) — instead of neutral Operator A examples, breaching operator-neutrality (policy 1) / identity-check. The segregated-account decision itself is compliant (ledger-derived balances, operator-enforced segregation, no negative balance).
entries.rationale: Current, coherent financial-segregation decision that preserves the wallet invariants (balances read from operator, double-entry to account_id, no application-side sub-ledger). REWRITE only to strip the non-neutral names ('DOA', 'BANZADMIN') and use Operator A / generic examples.

entries.title: BANZA v1.0 conformance level capability alignment
entries.rationale: The level model it states is the CURRENT canonical model (already open-trust: L3 = 'signed protocol metadata', no certificates; evidence-gated, no discretionary approval) — it does not contradict policy. But the whole ADR is framed as a correction of ADR-022 (its Context is 'ADR-022 established... used older naming... the two disagreed'), it 'Supersedes (in part) ADR-022', and it still cites the CA-era ADR-026. Because ADR-022 is recommended for DELETE, REWRITE this ADR to stand alone as THE canonical certification-level ADR: drop the ADR-022 correction narrative and dangling supersedes, and repoint ADR-026 -> ADR-040. It is the survivor that carries ADR-022's only live content.

entries.title: BANZA Certification Level Architecture
entries.removed_detail: CA + root-key + production-root + discretionary-approval: 'production BANZA Root key establishment' as a production blocker, BANZA-signed operator certificates with 90-day lifetime, 'Certificate must be signed by BANZA root key', BRL/PKI trust engine, dependency graph naming BANZA the 'certification authority', and 'BANZA CA issues certification'. All of this is removed architecture under ADR-038/039/040.
entries.contradiction_detail: Directly contradicts current policy 2 (NO CA, NO root-key ceremony, NO issued production certificates — trust is open, self-published, deterministically verified) and policy 3 (no discretionary/central human approval; it repeatedly assumes central certificate issuance and a 'certification authority'). The header already marks the trust/certificate model superseded by ADR-038.
entries.rationale: Fully superseded tombstone whose only remaining value is historical. Its CA/root-key/certificate/discretionary trust model is removed architecture, superseded by ADR-038 (open trust without CA), ADR-039 (self-publication + machine-verifiable conformance) and ADR-040 (federation trust without certificates). Its only still-'in force' content — the L0–L4 numbering and the L3 federation threshold — is fully restated by ADR-021 and by docs/governance/certification-boundary.md (authoritative for per-level capabilities and cumulative progression). No live rule survives that is not covered elsewhere. Clean-slate intent forbids keeping a large 'this was superseded' history file; Git history preserves it. DELETE.

entries.title: Transaction Proof Standard
entries.rationale: Current, operator-neutral standard ('No operator branding appears in this standard'). Signing is operator self-signing with rotatable key_id — consistent with the open trust / self-publication model (ADR-039), not a BANZA CA. Verification is deterministic against the ledger. No root-key, no discretionary approval, no operator-as-subject. Financial integrity preserved (append-only states, REVERSED never deleted). Minor wording ('the network's reference operator id') is not a contradiction — KEEP.

entries.title: Public Verification Pages
entries.rationale: Current, operator-neutral (uses correct 'Operator A' / 'operator.example' neutral examples, and makes the ADR-003 protocol/operator separation visible). Deterministic ledger-derived verification, no CA/root-key/discretionary/operator-as-subject, no new financial object. Preserves privacy and source-of-truth = ledger. KEEP; the reference-operator implementation note is correctly scoped to the operator repo.

entries.title: Interactive Financial Documents
entries.rationale: Current, coherent, and fully operator-neutral. Layers a document-presentation rule on ADR-023 without introducing any financial object; correctly keeps the ledger as sole source of truth. No CA, root-key, discretionary-approval, or operator-as-subject language. Uses 'reference operator' role and 'operator.example' placeholders correctly. Minor at most; keep as-is.

entries.title: Federation Trust Model
entries.removed_detail: CA (BANZA issues signed operator certificates), production-root (BANZA root signing key), discretionary-approval (mandatory human BANZA CA approval step before issuance), plus BRL/certificate lifecycle — the entire PKI-with-certificates trust model.
entries.contradiction_detail: Directly contradicts current policy #2/#3: there is NO CA, NO issued production certificates, NO root key, and NO discretionary operator approval. Trust is now an open model (operators self-publish signed metadata; anyone verifies deterministically).
entries.rationale: Explicitly and fully superseded; the doc itself states it is 'retained unchanged as the historical record.' Every live rule is restated by the current stack: the general trust model by ADR-038 (open protocol trust without CA) and cross-operator/federation trust by ADR-040 (federation trust evaluation without certificates). INV-TRUST-001..007 are certificate/CA invariants that no longer exist; any surviving cross-operator ledger guarantee is covered by INV-LEDGER-* and ADR-040. Under clean-slate intent this is a pure tombstone — DELETE; git history preserves it.

entries.title: BANZA Production Root Architecture
entries.removed_detail: production-root + root-key ceremony (offline root, 2-HSM custody, key manifest), CA (cert-issuing key signs operator certificates), and discretionary-approval ('BanzAI explains; BANZA CA authorizes'). The whole 'Production Root Architecture' is the removed CA/root machinery.
entries.contradiction_detail: Contradicts current policy #2 explicitly: NO BANZA root key ceremony, NO production root CA, NO issued production certificates. The 2026-06-19 clarification even 'approves' the root-key custody model that current policy has since removed.
entries.rationale: The entire ADR specifies the removed certificate-issuance PKI (root key + issuing keys + BANZA CA). Its frontmatter claims 'trust root key architecture carried forward,' but current policy states there is no root key ceremony/production root; whatever offline metadata-signing survives is now defined by ADR-038 (open trust model without CA), not by this ADR's cert/BRL/evidence issuing-key hierarchy. No live rule remains that ADR-038 does not cover. Retained only as historical record — DELETE.

entries.title: Private keys never reside on serving infrastructure
entries.removed_detail: root-key + CA framing: Context and Consequences are built entirely on the removed hierarchy (Root Key -> Key Manifest -> issuing keys -> operator certificates), and anchor to INV-ROOT-*/INV-TRUST-* and ADR-026 (all removed).
entries.contradiction_detail: Its scaffolding assumes the removed CA/root-key model (root ceremony, issuing keys, operator certificates, INV-ROOT-*/INV-TRUST-*, ADR-026). Under the open trust model these anchors no longer exist.
entries.rationale: The core operational-security decision survives and is genuinely live: the serving VM holds no private keys and does no signing; BANZA's own signing (of protocol metadata, per the ADR-038 open trust model) happens offline and the VM only serves signed public blobs. No current ADR restates this custody boundary, so it is not DELETE. But it must be rewritten off the removed CA scaffolding (drop root-ceremony/issuing-keys/operator-certificate/INV-ROOT/INV-TRUST/ADR-026 framing, re-anchor to ADR-038) and promoted from 'Proposed'.

entries.title: KYC stays operator policy; only Trust Assertions may federate
entries.contradiction_detail: The core decision (KYC = operator policy) is fully consistent with current policy. The only issue is a stale anchor: the reserved Trust Assertion is framed as extending ADR-026 (superseded) and 'verifiable via the federation trust chain' (certificate-chain phrasing).
entries.rationale: The decision is current, correct, and operator-neutral — a genuine boundary record keeping KYC out of the protocol, with a live reservation no other ADR restates, so not DELETE. But it references superseded ADR-026 as the federation anchor and uses certificate-'trust chain' language; re-anchor the future Trust Assertion to ADR-040 (federation trust evaluation without certificates) / open-trust-evaluation and drop the certificate-chain phrasing. Stale-reference cleanup = REWRITE.

entries.title: Environment Isolation: Sandbox vs Production
entries.rationale: Substance is current and sound — a real protocol decision (QR `environment` field ties to INV-QR-*; correctly assigns boot-guard/key-prefix to operator responsibility per ADR-003). But the frontmatter Author field reads 'the reference operator Organisation', a find-replace scrubbing artifact from a real operator name and wrong for a protocol ADR (should be 'BANZA Protocol'). Per the rubric, wrong frontmatter = REWRITE; the body only needs the author line corrected.

entries.title: Canonical verification routes and pre-production behaviour
entries.removed_detail: root-key/production-root (/.well-known/banza/root.json 'root key id', key-manifest 'active issuer keys'), CA (/certificates 'Issued production certificates index'), and BRL (/federation/revocation-list.json) — the published surface of the removed CA/root PKI. Also discretionary/CA note text ('a BANZA CA certifica') and pre-production M2/M3 milestone narrative.
entries.contradiction_detail: Publishes the removed CA anchors (root manifest/root key id, issuer key-manifest, issued-certificates index, BRL) and pre-production 'certificates depend on M2/M3' narrative; current policy has no root, no CA, no issued production certificates.
entries.rationale: Conflates a removed CA route table (root.json/key-manifest/certificates/revocation-list) with a still-valid surface decision — canonical honest, cache-bypassed JSON machine routes and a reserved /operators public registry (empty / Operador-Zero-only per current policy) plus /conformance/evidence. That HTTP-route canon and honesty guarantee are not fully restated by ADR-038/039/040, so not a pure DELETE. Rewrite: drop the CA/root/certificate/BRL routes and pre-production milestone narrative, keep and re-anchor the open-trust metadata + /operators registry + conformance-evidence routes to ADR-038/ADR-039/ADR-040, and resolve the 'Proposed' status.

entries.title: BanzAI as a subordinate, non-authoritative knowledge system
entries.removed_detail: CA/discretionary-approval: fixed truth framing 'a BANZA CA certifica após validação, dependente de M2/M3'. Also the retired 'subordinate / adjacent / auxiliary knowledge system' + 'Demo · knowledge system' framing, superseded by the native-protocol-agent / primary-interface architecture.
entries.contradiction_detail: 'BANZA CA certifies after validation' contradicts the no-CA policy; the 'subordinate knowledge system' framing contradicts current policy #5 (BanzAI is the PRIMARY human-operator interface / native protocol agent, ADR-041/049/050/054).
entries.rationale: Explicitly 'Superseded by ADR-041' and 'kept as a historical record.' Every live guardrail (non-normative, no certificate issuance, grounded/cited RAG, no production keys, index-only write) is carried forward and expanded by ADR-041 (native protocol agent) and ADR-049/050/054; the CA-certification framing is removed outright. Pure tombstone under clean-slate intent — DELETE; git history preserves it.

entries.title: Dedicated infrastructure, independent of any operator
entries.rationale: Decision is current and live (dedicated VPS in production), but the frontmatter status is stale 'Proposed' and the Context carries a pre-current 'historically hosted as a guest tenant on a reference operator's VM' framing. It has genuine protocol-architecture content (the operator-neutrality invariant applied to hosting), so it stays an ADR rather than MOVE: fix status->Accepted and trim the historical narrative to a current-only statement. No CA/discretionary/operator-as-subject content; aligned with operator neutrality.

entries.title: Dedicated PostgreSQL and encrypted off-VM backups
entries.removed_detail: CA: the Context lists 'certificates' among the public signed artifacts the DB must serve and index — an issued-certificate artifact that no longer exists under the open trust model.
entries.contradiction_detail: Treats 'certificates' as a served public protocol artifact, which assumes the removed CA/issued-production-certificate world (production_certificates=false; removed by ADR-038/039/040).
entries.rationale: Fix stale 'Proposed' status and purge the 'certificates' served-artifact reference. The no-financial-data / protocol-state-only rule overlaps the current ADR-042 (PostgreSQL data boundary) and should be deduplicated toward it, while the dedicated-instance + segregated-roles (banza_ro/banza_gov/banzai_rw) + encrypted-off-VM-backup rules remain live and are not restated by ADR-042. Not a clean MERGE (ADR-042 does not carry the deployment/backup mechanics) and not pure ops (the data boundary is architectural), so REWRITE.

entries.title: Deploy model: Docker Compose, pinned images, secrets outside Git
entries.scope_note: MOVE→infra/ deferred: deployment ops doc, current, no contamination. Relocation is churn without serving the mandate.
entries.rationale: Pure operational deployment mechanics — compose file, image-tag pinning, secrets location, systemd/ufw/unattended-upgrades, rollback runbook — with no protocol-invariant content. It configures how the reference deployment is wired, not a protocol rule. Current and non-contradictory, so no substantive rewrite is needed; relocate to infra/banza-network/ deployment docs (the canonical home of the reproducible bundle) rather than keep in the protocol ADR set.

entries.title: DNS and TLS: Cloudflare proxied, Full (strict), Origin Certificate
entries.removed_detail: CA: lists '/certificates' among the canonical machine routes requiring cache-bypass — a CA-era route (production_certificates=false).
entries.contradiction_detail: The /certificates machine route assumes issued production certificates, removed by the open-trust ADRs (038/039/040).
entries.scope_note: MOVE→infra/ deferred; REWRITE in place to remove the stale CA '/certificates' machine route (removed by ADR-038/039/040).
entries.rationale: Operational DNS/TLS/edge configuration (Cloudflare mode, Origin Certificate, redirects, cache rules, cutover discipline) with no protocol-architecture content; belongs in infra/banza-network/ deployment docs. On relocation, drop the stale '/certificates' machine-route reference. MOVE dominates; the CA residue is a cleanup to apply during the move, not the primary reason.

entries.title: Rust-first policy for official BANZA and BanzAI engines
entries.rationale: Current canonical policy (policy #4). Coherent, correctly named and numbered, Accepted status matches reality, and it explicitly preserves operator technology-neutrality while binding only official implementations. No CA/discretionary/operator-as-subject or stale-narrative content. Minor at most.

entries.title: Open Protocol Trust Model Without CA
entries.removed_detail: CA + discretionary-approval + production-root: it exhaustively describes the removed certificate issuance, the mandatory human approval gate, and the 'certification' issuing domain — but names each AS removed, in order to establish the current open model.
entries.rationale: This is the foundational ADR ESTABLISHING current policy #2 (no CA, Open Trust Evaluation), so it is emphatically not DELETE. But for a clean-slate current-only tree the text is dominated by removed-CA narrative (the 'what an attacker could do before' tables, exhaustive removed-vs-active comparisons) plus a completed M2.3 migration plan ('this is step 1; steps 2-7 remain') that is now dead project state, and it defines the 'Open Trust Evaluation' as SIX steps while ADR-040 defines the same-named evaluation as TEN checks — an internal inconsistency across the canonical set. Rewrite to state the current evaluation + INV-OTE + permanent boundary, relegate the removed-model polemic to git history, and reconcile the evaluation definition with ADR-040. It quotes the same canonical PT decision as ADR-039/040 (heavy overlap), but each carries distinct live rules, so REWRITE not MERGE.

entries.title: Operator Self-Publication and Machine-Verifiable Conformance
entries.removed_detail: discretionary-approval + CA: describes the removed mandatory human approval step, the human-gated review, the BANZA-issued proof-of-conformance artifact, the gatekeeper, and approval-gated registry listing — all named AS removed in the 'What this ADR removes' mapping.
entries.rationale: Current canonical (policy #2/#3: self-publication + deterministic machine-verifiable conformance, no discretionary approval), so not DELETE. But it re-quotes the identical canonical PT decision as ADR-038/040 and re-litigates the removed human-gate/certificate model at length (the defect narrative and the removed-vs-exists table). For a clean-slate current-only tree, keep the distinct live content — the 8-step self-publication path, the five machine-verifiable properties, and the absence-from-registry semantics — and strip the duplicated removed-model narrative. It is the operator-publishing side (distinct from ADR-038's verifier trust-model), so not fully covered elsewhere -> REWRITE, not MERGE.

entries.title: Federation Trust Evaluation Without Certificates
entries.removed_detail: CA + discretionary-approval + production-root: the 'Removed architecture — mapping' table names Verificacao Tripla, operator/production certificate, certified/approved operator, certificate authority as issuer, human-gated issuance/review, 90-day certificate expiry, the certification issuing domain and INV-TRUST-001..007 — all as removed.
entries.rationale: Current canonical federation-routing decision (policy #2), so not DELETE. But it defines the 'Open Trust Evaluation' as TEN checks while ADR-038 defines the same-named evaluation as SIX steps — a coherence defect the clean-slate must reconcile — and it carries a large 'Removed architecture — mapping' tombstone table plus a completed-M2.3 migration/ordering section that is dead project state. Rewrite to the current ten-check evaluation + INV-FEDEVAL + normative Boundary, reconcile the evaluation definition with ADR-038, and drop the removed-model mapping to git history. Distinct live content (ten checks, INV-FEDEVAL, endpoint/capability/freshness checks not enumerated in 038) -> REWRITE, not MERGE.

entries.title: BanzAI as Native Protocol Agent
entries.rationale: Foundational and fully current. Explicitly encodes current policy: no central admission authority, participation demonstrated by verifiable evidence not granted (pt 3), agent is non-normative and never certifies/approves (pts 4,5), AI output is never a protocol rule, and a strong rule-provenance clause (BanzAI cannot invent rules). It formally supersedes ADR-032 and is actively cited by ADR-044/049/054/055/056, so it anchors the live native-agent architecture. No CA/root-key/operator-as-subject language. Only nit: the parenthetical 'often surfaced as the Workbench interface' is slightly dated, but the Workbench still exists — not worth a rewrite. Correctly numbered and named.

entries.title: PostgreSQL as Protocol State Store, not a Financial Ledger
entries.rationale: Fully current and operator-neutral, backed by the live make postgres-data-boundary-check guard (per memory this ADR is the anchor whose repo-guards range gets bumped by new ADRs). Reaffirms policy pt 6: the financial invariants are rules the protocol DEFINES and verifies, not a ledger it operates (/operators=[], production_certificates=false, PASS is technical evidence not certification). The 'root manifest / key manifest (public issuer keys only, never private key material)' items are open-trust signed artifacts under ADR-038/039/040, not a CA or root-key ceremony — no removed architecture. Correctly numbered and named.

entries.title: License, Notice, Trademark and Open Governance Attribution
entries.rationale: Current, coherent, guard-backed (make license-notice-governance-check). Consistent with policy: 'the protocol remains open and independent of any private approval of operators' (pts 1,3) and separates creator/maintainer attribution from any control of the protocol or operators. Uses the neutral corporate creator name (allowed under ADR-002/ADR-043 identity rules), no commercial-operator brand, no CA. Correctly numbered and named.

entries.title: BanzAI Local Qwen Inference Runtime
entries.rationale: The core architecture is still current and is actively cited by ADR-055 and ADR-056 as the local-runtime + Rust-control basis (zero external calls), and it is fully policy-compliant (Qwen never normative/deciding/certifying — pt 4; Rust-first control — pt 4). But the text carries stale narrative that a clean-slate tree must not keep: it pins 'Qwen3-4B-GGUF Q4_K_M' as THE model (production later selected Qwen2.5-7B per M2.18B.3) and describes local_qwen as 'opt-in/preview' with 'mock/degraded remain the default' — false since ADR-048 activated local_qwen as the effective default (M2.8D/G). Rewrite to be model-version-agnostic and current-state, and consolidate the tuning children ADR-045/046/047 into it as the single canonical local-inference runtime ADR.

entries.title: BanzAI Local Qwen Latency Tuning and Default Readiness
entries.scope_note: Workflow suggested MERGE→044 (Qwen tuning consolidation). DEFERRED: current+correct+Accepted, not contamination; merging adds broken-ref/grounding risk for aesthetic gain. Out of scope for clean-slate (contamination/contradiction/tombstone) mandate.
entries.rationale: Pure incremental parameter-tuning of the ADR-044 runtime, not an independent architecture decision — exactly the kind of micro-ADR a clean-slate reconstruction consolidates. Its headline 256-token default is already superseded by ADR-047 (384), and its 'default readiness / mock stays default' gating is overtaken by ADR-048 (local_qwen live as effective default). The still-live rules (compact prompt, 60s timeout, ≤3 sources — cited by ADR-049 — curl healthcheck, warm-up contract) are not restated by any single other ADR, so DELETE is wrong; fold them into the consolidated ADR-044 runtime ADR.

entries.title: BanzAI: Disable Qwen Reasoning & Warm the System-Prompt Prefix
entries.rationale: Runtime-behavior tuning of the same local Qwen subsystem (its reasoning-off + zero-external-call properties are still cited by ADR-055). Reasoning-off and prefix warm-up are live rules but not a standalone architectural decision; in a current-only tree they belong consolidated in the ADR-044 local-inference runtime ADR rather than as a separate benchmark-cycle ADR. Not DELETE (rules are live and not restated elsewhere); not KEEP (fragmentary tuning of another ADR's subsystem).

entries.title: BanzAI: local_qwen 384-token Default Output Budget
entries.rationale: A single numeric default change to the ADR-044 runtime (it explicitly raises ADR-045's 256 to 384). 384 is the current live value (ADR-048 records it 'unchanged'), so the rule is live — but a whole standalone ADR for one output-budget constant is exactly what a clean-slate reconstruction folds in. Merge the current 384 value into the consolidated ADR-044 runtime ADR (carrying the supersession of ADR-045's 256).

entries.title: BanzAI: Qwen-first Grounded Routing & Deterministic Fallback
entries.scope_note: MERGE→056 deferred: current routing decision, not contamination; ADR-055/056 already carry the live essence — no contradiction, so no clean-slate need to remove.
entries.rationale: A genuine, policy-aligned architecture decision (deterministic Rust routing keeps boundary/identity answers off the model — pts 3,4; Qwen never decides). But the concrete route.rs 5-tier mechanism it defines was first extended by ADR-049 (protocol agent core) and then retired/subsumed by ADR-055 (Rust-first grounded synthesis, which 'retires the two-pass / model-entry interpretation architecture') and ADR-056 (Definitive Query Core — the current 'single Rust query authority' with the assurance layer). Its live essence (intent-vs-retrieval separation, Qwen-first grounded default, deterministic critical-boundary handling, deterministic post-validation fallback) is carried forward by ADR-055/056, so in a current-only tree it should be folded into ADR-056 rather than kept as the historical routing tombstone. Not KEEP (route.rs tier mechanism is stale); not DELETE (the routing rule survives, just relocated to the query-core ADR).

entries.title: BanzAI: Protocol Agent Core (operational intents, onboarding, documentary index)
entries.rationale: Role-decision is current and correct (non-normative operational agent; Rust owns retrieval/routing per ADR-037), but the body is dominated by superseded M2.8x mechanism (route.rs 14-label classifier, knowledge.js curated entries, pipeline.js BANZAI_DOC_ENRICH) that was rearchitected into the single banzai-query-core authority (ADR-056) and the single-pass synthesis (ADR-055); frontmatter is old-style (See also, no Milestone/Supersedes/Related). Not DELETE — it still holds a live artifact (banzai-doc-indexer / doc-index.json, consumed by ADR-056) and the operational-agent role. REWRITE: normalize frontmatter, trim the stale implementation narrative, keep the current operational-agent + documentary-indexer decision.

entries.title: BanzAI: Unified Same-Origin Public Interface
entries.rationale: Fully current and accurate (same-origin /banzai is live; subdomain retired; model not exposed) and a genuine architectural boundary. The only blemish is old-style frontmatter (See also / 'Shipped in M2.8E'), which does not rise to REWRITE. KEEP (minor).

entries.title: BanzAI: Per-Answer Execution-Path Metadata
entries.rationale: The honesty invariant (per-answer truthful label; external_model_called=false; cache never shown as live) is current and durable, but the enumerated label set is stale: ADR-056 introduced a closed reason-code enum (reason.rs) that generalises per-answer status, and the systematic 'Fallback seguro' degraded label was later removed (DEGRADED-FALLBACK fix). Old-style frontmatter. Not MERGE (distinct public-honesty decision not restated by ADR-056) and not MOVE (it is a real invariant, not mere docs). REWRITE: reconcile the label list with the ADR-056 reason-code model and normalize frontmatter.

entries.title: Operador Zero: reference payment-operator simulator
entries.removed_detail: Passing reference to 'the protocol's Trust Root' (from which the Demo Operator Root is 'separate') is CA/root-key-adjacent phrasing under the current open-trust model (ADR-038/039/040) and should be cleaned; it is not the ADR's subject.
entries.rationale: Core decision is current and central to policy #1 (Operador Zero is demo-only, never real/counted). But the text carries stale detail: the root-key-adjacent 'protocol's Trust Root' phrasing, and §12 'may be served first at /operador-zero while the subdomain is not active' — now stale, since zero.banza.network is LIVE and /operador-zero is 410 (per ADR-053). REWRITE to fix these and normalize frontmatter. Not DELETE/MERGE: it is the foundational Operador Zero decision, distinct from ADR-053's exclusivity policy.

entries.title: Operator Zero Only demo and example policy
entries.rationale: Fully current and directly enforces policy #1; coherent and well-scoped (three categories, abstract-placeholder carve-out, three CI guards, /operador-zero=410). It pairs with ADR-052 but encodes a distinct exclusivity policy, so it is not folded away. KEEP.

entries.title: BanzAI as the Primary Human-Operator Interface for the BANZA protocol
entries.contradiction_detail: Not in conflict with the provided policy itself, but the certificate framing ('production_certificates stays false', 'a conformance PASS is a local technical verification result, not a certificate', 'does not let BanzAI issue certificates or change /certificates', forbidden 'turning a PASS into a certificate') predates ADR-057, which replaces the absolute 'BANZA nunca certifica' stance with a qualified, engine-computed Technical Interoperability Certification while KEEPING BanzAI's 'never certifies'. ADR-057 explicitly mandates rewriting such surfaces to the qualified stance.
entries.scope_note: Workflow flagged REWRITE only vs the M2.19 certification DRAFT (set aside for M2.19). ADR-054's 'BanzAI never certifies / production_certificates=false' stance is CURRENT and correct pre-M2.19; rewriting it now would forward-reference a non-existent decision. The cert-qualification rewrite belongs to M2.19 after the cert ADR lands.
entries.rationale: The primary decision (BanzAI = primary but non-authoritative interface; policy #5) is fully current, correctly bounded, and has good frontmatter. REWRITE only to reconcile the certificate-related clauses with the now-current ADR-057 (BanzAI still never certifies; the Rust engines technically certify implementations; production certs currently pré-produção/0 active). Not DELETE/MERGE — it is the canonical primary-interface decision.

entries.title: Rust-First Grounded Synthesis for BanzAI
entries.rationale: Current, coherent embodiment of policy #4 (Rust-first; model out of the decision/certification path); good frontmatter; its four guards remain in force per ADR-056. Retiring the M2.18B.3 two-pass is an internal BanzAI redesign, not policy-removed architecture (no CA/root/discretionary/operator-subject). KEEP.

entries.title: Definitive Query Core, Canonical Knowledge Coverage and Production Assurance for BanzAI
entries.rationale: Current definitive query-core authority; coherent with policies #4/#5; good frontmatter; behavioral guards + test suite live. The multiple dated addenda (Semantic Task Fulfilment, TFG generalization, DFN-5..11 closure) are additive current content, not stale/tombstone narrative, so KEEP. A clean-slate could editorially fold the addenda into the body, but that is an editorial cleanup, not a classification change.

entries.title: Technical Interoperability Certification (without CA or discretionary operator approval)
entries.rationale: Newest ADR (M2.19) and the current canonical certification decision. Aligns with policy #2 (no CA/root/production-root; currently 0 active / pré-produção), #3 (deterministic, evidence-based, machine-verifiable; no discretionary approval), #4 (Rust engine is sole authority, Qwen never decides), and #1 (Operador Zero never counted). It preserves ADR-038/039, keeps the CA parts of ADR-022/026/027 removed, amends ADR-040, and requires RFC-0007. It is the ADR that qualifies the older absolute 'BANZA nunca certifica' framing (driving the ADR-054 REWRITE). KEEP.
